questions.prompt: A 50-trial pick benchmark has 40 successes. The gate needs a point estimate of at least 80 % and a lower 95 % Wilson bound of at least 68 %. What is the right conclusion?
options: Pass: the point estimate is exactly 80 %.
Pass: 50 trials is enough that the bound can be ignored.
Fail: the lower bound is about 67.0 %, so one more success would be needed; do not rerun until it passes.
Fail: the Wilson bound only applies above 100 trials.
questions.explanation: The Wilson interval for 40/50 is [0.670, 0.888]. 41/50 would give a lower bound of 0.692. Rerunning until a lucky pass is tuning on the test seeds.
questions.skillLabel: Judge success rates with the Wilson bound

questions.prompt: Your segmentation network reports mIoU 0.99 in its log but only 0.70 on the benchmark scenes. What is the most likely cause?
options: Train and test frames came from the same scenes (split by frame), so the test set leaked.
The learning rate was too small.
The network is too large for 128 x 96 input.
questions.explanation: Frames from one scene are near duplicates; splitting by frame lets the model memorise the test scenes. Split by scene seed and use different textures and lighting for the test.

questions.prompt: A camera image is 480 pixels high with a vertical field of view of 60 degrees. Focal length f_y in pixels, 1 decimal.
With f_x = 415.7 and c_x = 320, pixel column u = 400 at depth 0.5 m. Camera-frame X in metres, 4 decimals.
A joint moves 0.6 rad with v_max = 1.5 rad/s and a_max = 4 rad/s^2 using a quintic (peak v = 1.875 dq / T, peak a = 5.7735 dq / T^2). Shortest duration in seconds, 3 decimals.
questions.explanation: Velocity gives 0.75 s, acceleration gives sqrt(5.7735*0.6/4) = 0.931 s. The larger one binds.

questions.prompt: Why should every IK solve along a path start from the previous waypoint's joint angles?
options: It keeps the solution on one branch, so consecutive waypoints do not jump between elbow-up and elbow-down.
It removes the need for joint limits.
It makes damped least squares converge in exactly one step.
questions.explanation: A planar arm has two solutions for most targets. Starting from the previous solution keeps the iteration on the nearest branch; the test limits any joint step to 0.2 rad.

questions.prompt: Design a calibration and validation procedure for T_base_cam that would reveal an error of a few millimetres.
rubric: Collects at least 10 well-spread, non-collinear point pairs and fits the rigid transform (Kabsch/SVD, det = +1).
Validates on held-out points not used in the fit and reports RMS in millimetres.
Notes pixel size (about 1 mm at 0.4 m) and depth bias as the error budget, and re-checks after moving the camera.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
